# Fashionphile.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/fashionphile-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/fashionphile-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from Fashionphile.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Fashionphile for Second Hand Fashion Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-fashionphile)
- **Code:** [`fashionphile.py`](fashionphile.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product pages](results/products.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Fashionphile product pages
- Fashionphile search pages

## Functions

- `scrape_products(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape product data from Fashionphile product pages using the product API.
- `scrape_search(url, max_pages=10)` → `List[Dict]`

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import fashionphile


async def main():
    search = await fashionphile.scrape_search(
        url="https://www.fashionphile.com/shop/discounted/all",
        max_pages=3,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/products.json`](results/products.json): `id`, `title`, `body_html`, `vendor`, `product_type`, `created_at`, `handle`, `updated_at`, `published_at`, `template_suffix`, `published_scope`, `tags`, `variants`, `options`, `images`, `image`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `brand_name`, `product_name`, `condition`, `discounted_price`, `price`, `id`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`fashionphile.py`](fashionphile.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/fashionphile-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
